title: Sable and the Crown
premise: Ada Iversen, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the pieces he carves, has spent his life in a valley where magic cannot follow. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Ada learns the boy is a living key to Vhalen, a country erased from maps and memory by royal decree, now sealed behind a door that only opens in winter. Hunted by the Crown's memory-eaters, Ada must cross into the dead nation, guided by its lingering ghosts and by Sable, a disgraced royal executioner who chose exile over one last killing. To save the child, Ada must find the true door out of Vhalen before the long winter finishes falling — but leaving means the country dies forever, and staying means he does. In the end Ada gives his own memories of the valley as the toll, walking out with the boy while forgetting why he ever left home; Sable remains behind as Vhalen's final witness.
about_author: Ines Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border towns that no longer appear on modern maps. They write quiet, wintry fantasy about people who remember what institutions would rather erase.

chapters.title: The Boy at the Door
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. A snowbound night brings a silent child to Ada's workshop, clutching a carved bone token that hums when Ada touches it. The boy speaks words no living tongue knows, yet the dead in Ada's carvings recognize them. Emotional beat: uneasy wonder — Ada's ordered, magicless life cracks open for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. Consulting the valley's oldest skull-carving, Ada learns the boy's language belongs to Vhalen, a nation struck from record forty years ago. That same night, Crown riders arrive asking after 'unregistered speech.' Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve as Ada realizes the child is hunted.

chapters.title: Sable
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. The disgraced executioner, sent to retrieve the boy, instead finds she cannot raise her blade on him. She defects, bringing news that the memory-eaters are coming for the whole valley. Emotional beat: guilt and defiance entwined — Sable chooses treason in a single breath.

chapters.title: Out of the Valley
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. Fleeing through mountain passes where magic still cannot follow them, the trio outruns the first hunters. The boy begins drawing doors — dozens of them — in the snow. Emotional beat: fragile trust forming between Ada and Sable against a backdrop of relentless cold pursuit.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Crossing an unmarked ridge, they enter Vhalen's remnant: a frozen city where ghosts go about half-remembered lives and the sun hasn't risen in years. Sable recognizes the place from the executions she once carried out under false pretenses. Emotional beat: horror and grief — she helped bury this country alive.

chapters.title: The Memory-Eaters
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. The Crown's agents breach Vhalen, devouring ghosts street by street, and the boy's memories begin unraveling with each ghost consumed. Ada discovers the boy is not from Vhalen — he is Vhalen, its last unswallowed piece. Emotional beat: desperation; the stakes become the child's very self.

chapters.title: A Door Made of Names
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. In the drowned archive beneath the palace, the dead reveal the exit: a door keyed to every citizen's true name, which must be spoken aloud by someone who remembers them all. Sable confesses she kept a ledger of the condemned — the names survive. Emotional beat: terrible hope born from complicity.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. The memory-eaters corner them at the door as the final frost descends to seal Vhalen eternally. Speaking the names costs Sable her own past, and she falters — until Ada offers something else: his memories of the valley as substitute toll. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely, love declared without saying it.

chapters.title: The Toll
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. At the threshold, Ada pays — the valley, his workshop, every voice in every bone drains out of him. He pushes the boy through as the door narrows; Sable steps back into the dying city, choosing to remain as its witness so the names stay spoken. Emotional beat: heartbreak and completion intertwined.

chapters.title: Spring, Unremembered
chapters.summary: POV: Ada (after). Ada wakes in a spring valley he doesn't recognize, raising a child whose language he somehow understands anyway. Among his carvings he finds a bone token humming with a woman's voice, saying his name. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal — love outlasting memory, justice surviving outside all law.
